questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic difference between a typical cervical and thoracic vertebra?

options.text: Cervical vertebrae have longer spinous processes
Thoracic vertebrae foramina are bigger than the body
Thoracic vertebrae have tubercles on transverse processes

questions.explanation:
Typical cervical vertebrae are characterized by a foramen in the transverse process called the foramen transversarium. This transmits the vertebral artery and vein along with a branch from the cervicothoracic ganglion (vertebral nerve). Lateral parts of the transverse processes also contain anterior and posterior tubercles.

The source compares typical cervical and thoracic vertebrae in the retained table.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the number of bones in the vertebral column?
questions.explanation:
The vertebral column consists of 33 bones. The source lists 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 4 coccygeal vertebrae, while noting frequent variability and reported totals between 32 and 35.

The vertebral column is about 70 cm long in males and about 60 cm in females on average and functions in support, protection of the spinal cord and nerves, muscle attachment and hematopoiesis.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of 'vertebral segment-normal curvature' is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation:
The cervical-kyphosis pair is incorrectly matched. The cervical part normally demonstrates lordosis.

During embryonic life the body is flexed and has primary thoracic and pelvic curves, which are convex dorsally. After birth, functional muscle development produces secondary cervical and lumbar curves, which are concave forwards (lordosis).

Normal adult curvatures: cervical lordosis, thoracic kyphosis, lumbar lordosis, pelvic curve concave anteroinferiorly.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which statement regarding normal vertebral column curvature is false?

options.text: Thoracic curve develops when the infant starts walking.
Cervical curve appears when the infant starts supporting its head.
Lumbar curve appears when the child assumes the upright posture.

questions.correctAnswerText: Thoracic curve develops when the infant starts walking.
questions.explanation:
The thoracic curvature is a primary curve and develops during embryonic life itself; therefore the statement that it develops when the infant starts walking is false.

Primary thoracic and pelvic curves are convex dorsally. Secondary cervical curvature develops with muscles responsible for head extension; secondary lumbar curvature develops with muscles responsible for sitting upright and walking.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 32-year-old man suffered from iatrogenic trauma of the craniocervical joint following occipitocervical fusion and stabilization surgery. Which of the following structures are not included in this joint?
questions.explanation:
The craniocervical joints do not include the wings of the sphenoid. They connect the cranium to the vertebral column and include the atlanto-occipital and atlanto-axial joints; the bones involved include occipital condyles, atlas and axis.

The source notes occipitocervical fusion/stabilization as treatment for conditions including trauma, rheumatoid arthritis, congenital malformations, neoplasms and degeneration.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The movements at the ____________ joint permit a person to look to the right and left.
questions.explanation:
Movements at the atlanto-axial joint allow a person to look left and right.

The atlanto-axial joints include a median pivot joint between the dens and the ring formed by the anterior arch and transverse atlantal ligament, plus paired lateral synovial joints. Movement is almost exclusively rotation around the axis; normal range is about 40 degrees.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An orthopedician performing surgical decompression in a patient with cervical spondylosis accidentally damages the transverse atlantal ligament. What is this a component of?
questions.explanation:
The transverse atlantal ligament is a component of the cruciform ligament at the atlanto-axial joints.

Cruciform ligaments are cross-shaped. The horizontal component is the transverse atlantal ligament, attached on each side to lateral masses of atlas and retaining the dens. The vertical component is formed by superior and inferior longitudinal ligaments.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 44-year-old man is brought to the casualty with a suspected whiplash injury following a road traffic accident. Which ligament would be injured in this condition?
questions.explanation:
The clinical scenario is suggestive of whiplash injury, in which the anterior longitudinal ligament of the spine is damaged.

Whiplash is a cervical acceleration-deceleration injury with hyperextension followed by recoil flexion. The anterior longitudinal ligament is a strong band along the anterior vertebral bodies, extending from the basilar occiput to upper sacrum and attaching at the anterior tubercle of C1 and body of C2.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: MRI of a 54-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis showed tectorial membrane thickening. This structure is derived from which of the following ligaments?
questions.explanation:
Membrana tectoria (tectorial membrane) is the cranial continuation of the posterior longitudinal ligament.

The posterior longitudinal ligament lies in the vertebral canal on the posterior surfaces of vertebral bodies, extends from the axis to the sacrum, and above the axis continues as membrana tectoria to the foramen magnum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 75-year-old cachexic man presents with nagging back pain in the lumbar region that shoots down his right leg. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer 2 months back. Which of the following movements is anatomically restricted in the lumbar region?
questions.explanation:
Rotation is anatomically restricted in the lumbar region. The source clinical vignette is suggestive of carcinoma prostate metastatic to the lumbar spine.

Flexion is accompanied by relaxation of the anterior longitudinal ligament and compression of the anterior intervertebral discs; flexion is most effective in the thoracic region. Extension is greater in cervical and lumbar regions, lateral flexion is accompanied by axial rotation, and axial rotation is greatest in the cervical region at the atlanto-axial joint. Lumbar regions have very little rotation.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An army personnel complains of lower backache following a bullet wound. On examination, she has sensory loss on the ipsilateral side below the level of the lesion. What is false about the visceral landmarks of the affected structure?

options.text: Heart lies in T5-T8 in recumbent position.
SVC enters right atrium at T5.
Azygos vein enters SVC at T5.
Hemiazygos vein crosses left to right at T5.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hemiazygos vein crosses left to right at T5.
questions.explanation: The scenario is suggestive of Brown-Sequard syndrome due to vertebral-column injury. The false landmark is that the hemiazygos vein crosses from left to right at T5; the source states it crosses at T8 (and not T5).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The following procedure was planned for a patient with a suspicion of Guillain-Barré syndrome. What is not pierced during this procedure?
questions.explanation:
A lumbar puncture is planned for suspected Guillain-Barré syndrome. The posterior longitudinal ligament is not pierced during lumbar puncture.

Structures pierced during lumbar puncture, in order, are skin, subcutaneous tissue, supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura mater and arachnoid mater.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: You are asked to auscultate a patient presenting with chronic cough. Which of the following is not a boundary of the triangle of auscultation?
questions.explanation:
Serratus anterior is not a boundary of the triangle of auscultation. This region has fewer impedances between the stethoscope and lungs and permits better auscultation of the patient.

Boundaries: medially trapezius lateral border; laterally scapula medial border; inferiorly latissimus dorsi upper border. The floor includes the 5th and 7th ribs, 6th intercostal space and rhomboid major.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The muscle marked by the arrow in the image below is innervated by the ________.

options.text: From the dorsal rami of C1

questions.explanation:
The muscle marked by the arrow is levator scapulae, which is innervated by the dorsal scapular nerve.

The source table lists selected appendicular muscles of the back and their nerve supply: trapezius-accessory nerve, latissimus dorsi-thoracodorsal nerve, levator scapulae-dorsal scapular nerve, rhomboid major/minor-dorsal scapular nerve. It also notes the suprascapular nerve supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus, while subscapular nerves supply teres major and subscapularis.
